primary_claim: Changing the Toy-Models-of-Superposition loss to reconstruct only the active (target) feature, rather than the full output, allows superposition without any element-wise non-linearity (no ReLU), packing dozens of features into two dimensions and showing that neither 'feature count is bounded by near-orthogonal directions' nor 'non-linearities are required for superposition' holds universally

effect.metric: fraction of features classified accurately by the toy model
effect.value: at sparsity p=0.95, 31 of 100 features represented accurately; accuracy improves with sparsity (more than 50 of 100 features accurate at p=0)

contradicts_or_qualifies: Toy Models of Superposition (Elhage et al. 2022)'s claims that feature count is bounded by near-orthogonal directions and that superposition doesn't occur in linear models / requires non-linearities; this post shows neither holds universally
limitations_stated: not confident in these findings; produced quickly (~30 hours) and don't reflect the rigor of a paper or preprint
experiments focus on representing features rather than datapoints, unlike related double-descent work
results depend heavily on the specific loss function and sparsity assumptions and may not generalize to other toy-model setups
as sparsity parameter p increases, it becomes much harder to get results as clean as the p=0.95 example shown
quote: we use a loss function that focuses only on reconstructing active features and find that this variation allows us to squeeze dozens of features into two dimensions without a non-linearity.
